title: The rotational ladder of CO
caption: Rotational energies go as E_J = hBJ(J + 1), so the gaps grow: a J → J − 1 photon has f = 2BJ. The lines are evenly spaced by 2B = 115 GHz: 115, 230, 345 GHz: microwaves, with 345 GHz (0.87 mm) already in the far infrared.
alt: Rotational energy levels of carbon monoxide for J = 0 to 3, with gaps growing upward and transitions at 115, 230 and 345 gigahertz.
description: Transitions J → J − 1: 115 GHz, 230 GHz, 345 GHz, spaced by 2B.
From the spacing, the moment of inertia and then the bond length (about 0.113 nm) follow.
